summary: Added opt-in host-f64 vector ray tracing through bounded centered spherical and plane refracting surfaces with Snell refraction, aperture vignetting, explicit miss/TIR statuses, optical path length, and image-plane centroid/RMS spot quantities.
limitations: Centered sequential spherical/plane refracting surfaces only; no native ZMX parsing or compatibility is claimed.
Decenters, tilts, aspheres, coatings, reflection, gradient-index media, diffraction, ray aiming, and material dispersion are unsupported and rejected.
Host f64 only; explicit GPU requests return Unsupported, while auto selects host for this operation.
Surface apertures are circular semi-diameters; rays are traced in listed order and each valid ray must travel forward.
Image-plane spot metrics use only rays that reach the image plane; per-ray statuses identify vignetting, invalid intersection geometry, and total internal reflection.

summary: Added an opt-in host-f64 discrete Fourier magnitude of a uniformly sampled nonnegative line-spread function, normalized by its total intensity and evaluated at requested spatial frequencies.
limitations: Host-f64 only; explicit CUDA requests fail closed.
Uses a finite uniformly sampled LSF and rectangular discrete-sum quadrature; no interpolation, window correction, or continuous-domain reconstruction.
This is a local image-analysis operation, not OpticStudio integration or a full lens-system diffraction analysis.
Accepts 2..=4096 finite nonnegative samples and 1..=128 frequencies within the sample Nyquist interval.
Reports incoherent MTF magnitude only; phase and polychromatic weighting are not computed.

summary: Added bounded host-f64 weighted least-squares fitting of sampled wavefront values to orthonormal OSA/ANSI-indexed Zernike modes, with weighted RMS residual and fail-closed sample/rank checks.
limitations: This is a sampled wavefront fit, not an OpticStudio integration or native lens-file workflow.
The mode list uses zero-based OSA/ANSI ordering (negative m sine, m=0, positive m cosine); it is not an OpticStudio Noll-numbered coefficient vector.

Samples are [rho, theta radians, wavefront value, positive weight] on the unit disk; it does not perform ray tracing, pupil sampling, chief-ray referencing, subaperture transforms, or annular-pupil fitting.
Host-f64 only; terms are limited to 1..10 and samples to terms..4096; GPU requests are rejected.

opticStudioFeature: Sellmeier material dispersion and derived group index
summary: Added an opt-in analytic bulk group-index result derived from multi-term Sellmeier coefficients, with strict coefficient/wavelength/selector validation and honest host-f64 provenance.
limitations: Uses real, lossless, isotropic multi-term Sellmeier material coefficients only.
Computes bulk group index from the local wavelength derivative; it does not model waveguide modal dispersion, absorption, temperature/pressure shifts, or OpticStudio catalog fitting.
Host-f64 operation only; explicit CUDA requests are rejected.
Does not parse AGF files or claim native OpticStudio compatibility.

opticStudioFeature: Model Glass relative partial dispersion and dPgF characterization
summary: Added an opt-in glass-partial-dispersion operation that computes Vd, PgF, the reference normal-line PgF, and dPgF from validated g/F/d/C refractive indices, with host-f64 provenance and fail-closed CUDA admission.
limitations: This is a material-characterization calculation, not native OpticStudio integration or a material catalog lookup.
Requires finite indices in (1, 4] with conventional normal-dispersion ordering ng > nF > nd > nC.
Uses the documented linear normal-line approximation PgF = 0.6438 - 0.001682*Vd; it does not estimate refractive index at arbitrary wavelength or reproduce the proprietary Model Glass formula.
The new operation supports host f64 only; explicit CUDA requests return Unsupported.

opticStudioFeature: Material Catalog refractive-index versus wavelength inspection (Dispersion Diagram analogue)
summary: Added opt-in dispersion-curve selector evaluating the existing Cauchy approximation at an explicit bounded, strictly increasing wavelength list; output reports host-f64 provenance.
limitations: Evaluates only n=A+B/λ²; it does not load OpticStudio catalogs or implement other glass dispersion formulas.
Host-f64 operation only; explicit CUDA requests fail closed.
Requires 2–128 finite, strictly increasing wavelengths in 0.1–10 µm and a finite positive resulting index.
This local material calculation is not an OpticStudio-compatible vendor workflow.

summary: Adds opt-in aperture-design conversion among effective focal length, entrance pupil diameter, image-space F/#, and image-space NA, with strict bounds and honest host-f64 provenance; preserves the existing default NA/fiber path.
limitations: First-order infinite-conjugate sizing only; no prescription parsing, pupil magnification, vignetting, ray tracing, or paraxial solver.
Assumes consistent lens units for effective focal length and entrance pupil diameter.
The new operation runs on host-f64; explicit GPU requests fail closed.
Only one of entrancePupilDiameter or imageSpaceFNumber is accepted; numeric inputs are restricted to documented finite engineering bounds.

summary: Added opt-in host-f64 normalized on-axis coherent pupil intensity from bounded sampled OPD and optional amplitude weights; reports explicit host provenance and fails closed for CUDA requests.
limitations: Input is a one-dimensional list of sampled pupil OPD values in metres, not a 2-D pupil grid or imported OpticStudio data.
Computes the discrete on-axis coherent intensity ratio only; it does not propagate a field, construct a PSF, search for its peak, remove piston/tilt/focus, or model pupil geometry.
Optional weights are nonnegative amplitude weights, not irradiance weights; equal implicit weights assume equal-area samples.
Host f64 only; explicit CUDA requests return Unsupported. This is not an OpticStudio implementation or a substitute for its FFT/Huygens PSF analyses.

summary: Added an opt-in uncoated lossless isotropic-interface operation returning s/p power reflectance and transmittance, refracted angle, and explicit TIR coefficients; the operation reports host-f64 provenance and rejects GPU selection.
limitations: Host f64 only; backend cuda is rejected and auto uses this host implementation.
Models a single uncoated, lossless, isotropic interface with real positive refractive indices in (0,100] and incident angle in [0,pi/2).
Does not model complex indices, absorption, coatings, multilayers, birefringence, Jones vectors, or full OpticStudio polarization transport.
This is a local Fresnel calculation, not OpticStudio integration or a claim of vendor-equivalent ray tracing.

summary: Adds an opt-in host-f64 Stokes/Mueller chain for bounded ideal on-axis linear retarders and diattenuating polarizers while preserving the legacy Brewster/Malus default response.
limitations: Ideal Jones-equivalent/Mueller elements only; axes and retardance are on-axis scalar quantities.
No ray geometry, oblique-incidence vector fields, Fresnel interfaces, coating tables, birefringent ray splitting, or OpticStudio file compatibility.
At most 16 elements; retarder retardance is limited to [0,2pi] and axes to [-pi,pi] radians.
Host-f64 only; explicit CUDA requests fail closed because no polarization-chain CUDA kernel exists.

summary: Added an opt-in host-f64 material-transmission operation that converts sampled reference-thickness internal transmission values to per-mm transmission, linearly interpolates in wavelength, and scales to the requested material path length.
limitations: Computes internal bulk transmission only; surface reflections, coatings, polarization, and ray tracing are not modeled.
Requires 1 to 128 strictly increasing wavelength rows and rejects wavelengths outside the supplied table instead of extrapolating.
Host-f64 implementation only; explicit CUDA requests fail closed.
Implements the documented material-table interpolation behavior and does not read OpticStudio catalogs or claim to execute OpticStudio.

summary: Added an opt-in host-f64 planar-boundary Fresnel power calculation for s, p, and unpolarized illumination, including total internal reflection, energy balance, strict input admission, and explicit backend provenance.
limitations: Models one lossless, isotropic planar interface only; it is not a complete OpticStudio polarization ray trace.
Does not model coatings, complex refractive index or absorption, multilayer phase, Jones vectors, birefringence, or ray geometry.
Host-f64 only; explicit CUDA/GPU requests fail closed and auto reports host provenance.

summary: Added an opt-in sampled 1D hard slit stop to a Gaussian complex field, reports transmitted fraction and propagates the clipped field with the existing paraxial split-step solver; host-f64 provenance is explicit.
limitations: This is a local sampled 1D slit-aperture POP-style calculation, not an OpticStudio workflow or ZMX implementation.

The aperture is an ideal binary amplitude stop centered on the periodic transverse grid; 2D/circular apertures, surface sequences, coatings, and automatic propagation-method selection are unsupported.
Propagation is paraxial split-step Fourier on a host-f64 periodic grid; GPU requests fail closed and the new operation is bounded to n and steps no greater than 512.

opticStudioFeature: Physical Optics Propagation (Gaussian beam free-space analysis)
summary: Added an opt-in host-f64 fundamental Gaussian q-parameter report for detector planes, including beam radius, wavefront curvature, Rayleigh range, and Gouy phase.
limitations: Host-f64 calculation only; explicit CUDA/GPU requests fail closed.
Models a paraxial fundamental Gaussian beam in homogeneous free space only; no surfaces, apertures, media transitions, aberrations, or vendor file compatibility.
Lengths are SI metres and z values are measured from the beam waist.
At the waist plane radiusOfCurvature is null and planarWavefront is true.

summary: Added opt-in lossless dielectric-interface Fresnel analysis for s, p, and unpolarized reflectance/transmittance, transmitted angle, and total internal reflection. The calculation uses host f64 and is an interface model only.
limitations: Single planar boundary between positive real refractive indices; absorbing, anisotropic, and birefringent materials are unsupported.
No thin-film or vendor coating stack, Jones-vector phase tracking, ray tracing, or OpticStudio execution is implemented.
New operation is host-f64 only; explicit CUDA requests return unsupported.

opticStudioFeature: Physical Optics Propagation Gaussian beam definition and free-space beam metrics
summary: Added opt-in analytic paraxial Gaussian beam propagation in a homogeneous medium, reporting beam radius, wavefront curvature, Gouy phase, Rayleigh range, and far-field half-angle at bounded requested planes, with host-f64 provenance and fail-closed input/backend checks.
limitations: Analytic scalar paraxial Gaussian-beam propagation through a uniform medium only; it does not implement OpticStudio POP or reproduce diffraction-grid propagation through a lens system.
Uses SI metres and a constant positive phase refractive index; no apertures, aberrations, polarization, absorption, astigmatism, or wavelength-dependent material model.
Host f64 only; explicit GPU backend requests fail closed. Backend auto uses the host implementation.

summary: Added opt-in scalar Fraunhofer irradiance samples for a uniformly illuminated coherent array of rectangular slits, with bounded inputs, explicit host-f64 provenance, and fail-closed GPU admission.
limitations: Scalar Fraunhofer approximation for an ideal uniform coherent rectangular-slit array; not a native OpticStudio analysis or file workflow.
Does not model polarization, Fresnel coefficients, aberrations, partial coherence, nonuniform illumination, detector pixel integration, or near-field propagation.
Host-f64 only; explicit GPU requests are rejected.

summary: Adds an opt-in host-f64 scalar Airy transmission spectrum over an ordered vacuum-wavelength sample list, returning round-trip phase and normalized transmission per sample. Existing FSR and reflectivity methods retain their behavior.
limitations: Scalar lossless Airy teaching model only; assumes a uniform medium and equal mirrors represented by the coefficient of finesse F.
Wavelengths are vacuum meters and must be finite, positive, strictly increasing, and limited to 256 samples.
Host-f64 only for this operation; CUDA and auto backend selections are rejected.
Does not model polarization, coating dispersion, absorption, scattering, finite beam propagation, or a native OpticStudio system/workflow.

opticStudioFeature: Physical Optics Propagation (POP) coherent irradiance cross-section
summary: Added opt-in algo=detector-line to sample equal-amplitude two-beam coherent irradiance across a centered line detector with a linear optical-path-difference gradient; reports host-f64 sample irradiances and sampled visibility.
limitations: Host-f64 only; explicit GPU requests fail closed.
Local scalar equal-amplitude two-beam interference model; not native OpticStudio integration or full POP propagation.
No diffraction, propagation between surfaces, apertures, polarization, coatings, spectral bandwidth, or arbitrary wavefront model.
Admission bounds: 2–4096 pixels, pixel pitch 1e-9–1e-2 m, wavelength 1e-7–1e-4 m, path difference within ±1 m, I0 0–1e12, and pathSlope within ±2.

summary: Added an opt-in coherent-detection operation that sums up to 256 scalar ray fields by amplitude and phase into one detector-bin intensity, reports the corresponding incoherent sum and interference contribution, and marks host-f64 provenance. Existing Mach-Zehnder defaults and CUDA operation remain unchanged.
limitations: This is scalar coherent accumulation into a single detector bin; it does not implement OpticStudio or read its project files.
It omits polarization, coating response, ray splitting, propagation, detector geometry and wavelength-dependent effects.
Each ray amplitude is a finite nonnegative scalar field magnitude; phase is finite radians; input is limited to 1 through 256 rays.
The new operation is host-f64 only; GPU requests fail closed.

summary: Added opt-in fresnel-oblique evaluation for an uncoated lossless dielectric interface, reporting S/P power reflection and transmission, unpolarized reflectance, refraction, and total internal reflection; calculations report host-f64 provenance.
limitations: Single planar interface between real, positive refractive indices; indices are bounded to [1e-6, 1e6].
No coatings, absorption, complex refractive indices, Jones-vector propagation, birefringence, or multi-surface ray tracing.
theta is measured from the surface normal in radians and must lie in [0, pi/2].
The new operation is host-f64 only; explicit CUDA requests fail closed.

summary: Added opt-in planar lossless total-internal-reflection Artmann shift calculations for s, p, and equally weighted unpolarized light; legacy default path is unchanged.
limitations: Single planar, isotropic, lossless interface under total internal reflection only.
Uses a scalar Artmann phase-gradient displacement; finite beam profiles, coatings, birefringence, Jones-vector orientation, and full sequential ray tracing are not modeled.
CUDA requests fail closed because the new operation is host-f64 only; backend auto uses host-f64.
Unpolarized output is the equal-power arithmetic mean of s and p centroid shifts.

summary: Added opt-in host-f64 analysis of an ideal on-axis Faraday rotator followed by a linear analyzer, reporting rotated linear-polarization angle and Malus-law transmitted power fraction; the existing scalar-angle path and defaults are preserved.
limitations: Host-f64 only; CUDA requests fail closed.

Ideal normal-incidence linear-polarization and analyzer model using Malus' law; no complex Jones phases, coatings, Fresnel loss, oblique rays, birefringence, or native OpticStudio surface/workflow compatibility.
Input and analyzer angles are limited to [-360, 360] degrees.

opticStudioFeature: Non-sequential ray interception and detector footprint analysis
summary: Added opt-in footprint method that intersects a bounded ray bundle against one existing analytic primitive and reports per-ray intersections, hit/miss counts, unweighted intercept fraction, hit centroid, and hit bounds. Host-f64 provenance is preserved; explicit GPU requests fail closed for this unsupported method and auto uses host.
limitations: Local analytic primitive intersection only; it does not implement OpticStudio or claim ZMX compatibility.
Each ray is tested against one primitive independently; no scene object ordering, reflection, refraction, scattering, ray splitting, or detector pixel binning.
The intercept fraction gives every supplied ray equal weight and is not a flux or irradiance estimate.
Ray bundles are host-f64 only and limited to 50,000 rays; explicit CUDA/GPU selection is unsupported.
Available primitives retain their existing scope: sphere, finite cylinder, disk, rectangle, and axis-aligned cube; no imported CAD or aspheric objects.
The result is geometric intersection/footprint data, not a complete OpticStudio analysis report.

summary: Added an opt-in nearest ray/triangle query over parsed OBJ or ASCII PLY geometry. Returns physical hit distance and point, triangle index, barycentrics, winding-derived geometric normal, and front-face flag; parser defaults and outputs are preserved.
limitations: Host-f64 only; CUDA requests continue to fail closed.
Intersects only triangle faces from the module's supported OBJ and ASCII PLY subset; no OpticStudio file/API compatibility is claimed.
Uses double-sided Möller–Trumbore geometric intersections without optical material, refraction, reflection, scattering, transforms, or full non-sequential ray-history simulation.

summary: Added a bounded visibility method that checks up to 256 finite source-to-detector segments against the existing opaque BVH/octree primitive scene and reports the first blocker; detector endpoints are excluded from blocker hits.
limitations: Opaque straight-line geometric visibility only; does not model ray splitting, scattering, reflection, refraction, flux, or detector irradiance.
Scene primitives are host-f64 triangles, spheres, or axis-aligned boxes; this is not an OpticStudio file interface or vendor ray trace.
At most 256 primitives and 256 source-to-detector queries; CUDA requests remain unsupported and fail closed.

opticStudioFeature: Non-sequential 3D component placement and layout validation
summary: Adds method=clearance to flatten a bounded optical assembly and report conservative world-AABB intersections, Euclidean separations, minimum-clearance violations, and an overall pass flag. Pairwise evaluation is capped at 1,024 instances; this is a host-f64 broad-phase envelope check, not OpticStudio ray tracing or exact surface interference analysis.
limitations: Uses axis-aligned bounding boxes transformed from prototype bounds; rotated envelopes can conservatively report interference without exact solid intersection.
Does not model optical surfaces, materials, ray propagation, scattering, sources, or detectors.
Pairwise clearance admission is limited to 1,024 flattened instances and reports host-f64 provenance only.

opticStudioFeature: Sellmeier 1 glass dispersion and wavelength-dependent uncoated interface response
summary: Adds the opt-in sellmeier-spectrum method: evaluates a three-term Sellmeier 1 index over a bounded wavelength list and reports Snell refraction and uncoated s/p Fresnel reflectance/transmittance per wavelength.
limitations: Host-f64 analytic helper only; explicit GPU requests return unsupported.
Requires exactly three coefficient pairs using Sellmeier 1 form and wavelength units in micrometers.
Models isotropic lossless bulk index and a single smooth uncoated interface; no glass catalog lookup, absorption, coatings, ray trace, or OpticStudio execution.
Accepts at most 100000 wavelength samples and rejects Sellmeier poles and non-positive n squared.

summary: Adds an opt-in plane-parallel dispersive plate operation that reports wavelength-dependent exit angle, lateral shift, internal and excess optical path, and lossless incoherent multi-bounce transmission/reflection. Existing dispersive-interface behavior remains the default.
limitations: Host-f64 only for the new operation; explicit CUDA/GPU requests fail closed and auto reports host provenance.
Ideal lossless isotropic uncoated plate with parallel planar faces and the same outside refractive index on both sides.

Uses geometric ray optics and sums incoherent internal reflections; phase-coherent etalon fringes, coatings, absorption, roughness, birefringence and curved/decentered/aspheric surfaces are unsupported.

opticStudioFeature: Coating polarization phase and diattenuation analysis
summary: Added opt-in method-algo-thinfilm-polarization to report reflected/transmitted p-minus-s phase and signed power diattenuation from the multilayer coating amplitudes; legacy method/default remain unchanged.
limitations: Uses the existing isotropic planar characteristic-matrix stack and its s/p eigenamplitudes; it is not a full OpticStudio coating catalog or ray-trace integration.
Phase difference is arg(p)-arg(s), wrapped to [-pi, pi]; it is null if either compared amplitude is exactly zero.
Power diattenuation is (Pp-Ps)/(Pp+Ps), with null when the compared total power is zero.
New polarization analysis runs on host-f64; explicit GPU selection fails closed and auto reports the host backend.

summary: Added an opt-in complex 2x2 Jones-matrix element and its equivalent Mueller transform, allowing Jones field operations to participate in existing Stokes cascades with explicit finite/shape validation and host-only backend provenance.
limitations: Jones surface uses a 2D transverse field and is an idealized normal-incidence model; it omits off-axis longitudinal field components, Fresnel coefficients, beam splitting, birefringence, and coatings.
Complex matrix components are supplied as finite [real,imag] pairs.
The implementation is host-f64 only; CUDA requests fail closed.
This is a local polarization calculation and does not run or claim compatibility with the OpticStudio application or file formats.

opticStudioFeature: Non-sequential detector radiometric and photometric outputs
summary: Added method-detector-photometry to integrate sampled spectral irradiance into W/m² and photopic lux using the built-in analytic CIE y-bar approximation scaled by 683 lm/W; optional areaM2 yields total luminous flux in lumens. Host f64 only.
limitations: Input is already sampled spectral irradiance in W/m²/nm; ray accumulation, detector geometry, spectral ray tracing, and detector file formats are outside scope.
The photopic response uses the module's analytic CIE y-bar approximation normalized at 555 nm, not a tabulated CIE dataset.
Explicit CUDA/GPU requests fail closed because this operation has no device kernel.
Optional areaM2 assumes uniform irradiance over the supplied detector area.

opticStudioFeature: Non-sequential Detector Color spectral source mixing and tristimulus reporting
summary: Added opt-in spectrum-mix operation that adds up to 32 weighted source spectral power distributions sampled on one shared wavelength grid and reports aggregate CIE XYZ, xyY, sRGB, radiant power, and photopic luminous flux using the existing trapezoidal integrator. Preserved all prior operations and defaults; host-f64 only with GPU requests failing closed.
limitations: This is a local sampled-spectrum colorimetry operation, not an OpticStudio integration or native Detector Color implementation.
All components must use the same strictly ascending wavelength grid; each component supplies non-negative spectral power and a non-negative scalar weight.
The aggregate represents incoherent spectral-power addition and does not model ray propagation, source overlap by detector pixel, angular response, wavelength-dependent optics, or noise.
Host f64 only; CUDA/GPU requests are unsupported and fail closed. The mix is bounded to 32 components and 4096 wavelength samples.

opticStudioFeature: single-interface polarized Fresnel reflection / Jones polarization analysis
summary: Added opt-in method-fresnel-jones: apply exact complex s/p Fresnel reflection coefficients to a local-basis complex Jones state and report reflected state, phase, and power, including total internal reflection.
limitations: Models one planar isotropic interface only; no thin-film coating stack or OpticStudio coating catalog.
Jones components are in the local plane-of-incidence [s,p] basis; global polarization reference conventions and full sequential ray polarization transport are not modeled.
Host-f64 only; CUDA/GPU requests fail closed.
No claim of native OpticStudio/ZMX compatibility.

opticStudioFeature: measured tabular BSDF scatter polar analysis
summary: Added opt-in scatter-polar analysis that samples the existing host-f64 measured BSDF at a bounded list of outgoing polar angles for one fixed incident direction and azimuth.
limitations: Requires a caller-supplied decoded dense RGB table; Zemax BSDF file parsing is not implemented.
Reports a host-f64 polar slice and does not execute OpticStudio or model detector ray tracing.
Only outgoing polar angles in [0, pi/2] are accepted; at most 512 samples per request.

opticStudioFeature: Anisotropic bulk scattering in a finite homogeneous slab
summary: Added opt-in method-delta-eddington: scales homogeneous slab scattering by (1-g²), retains absorption, then reports finite-slab two-flux reflectance/transmittance and absorption with host-f64 provenance.
limitations: Delta-Eddington scaling followed by Kubelka–Munk two-flux closure is approximate; it is not an OpticStudio ray trace or vendor-compatible workflow.
Homogeneous finite slab only; no spatial geometry, wavelength change, polarization, ray splitting, or detector model.
Asymmetry parameter is bounded to [-0.95, 0.95]; GPU execution is unsupported and rejected.

summary: Added an opt-in Rayleigh bulk wavelength method that scales the reference mean free path by (wavelength/referenceWavelength)^4 and reports Beer-Lambert scattered and unscattered probabilities over a homogeneous path length. Legacy default HG behavior is preserved.
limitations: Deterministic homogeneous-volume attenuation calculation; does not trace or sample rays in an OpticStudio non-sequential system.
Wavelength and referenceWavelength must share units; meanFreePath and volumeLength must share units.
Does not model the OpticStudio DLL transmission parameter, particle properties, scattering polarization, or Mie scattering.
Host f64 only; GPU requests fail closed.
Implementation follows the documented wavelength scaling and Beer-Lambert probabilities; it is not a native OpticStudio integration.

summary: Adds an opt-in geometric-spot method that projects bounded deterministic circular-aperture samples into the thin-lens image-plane defocus spot and reports geometric diameter plus sampled RMS radius.
limitations: Centered ideal thin lens with paraxial circle-of-confusion geometry only; not a multi-surface OpticStudio sequential ray trace.
The circular point cloud omits aberrations, vignetting, field-dependent pupil mapping, diffraction, wavelength dependence, coatings, and detector pixel integration.
Spot samples are deterministic radial aperture samples; sampled RMS radius depends on the selected sample count.
Host f64 implementation only; GPU backends remain unsupported.
A geometric-spot request requires 1 to 256 positive finite object distances and supports 1 to 64 spot samples.

summary: Added an opt-in area-emitter ray method that samples existing rectangle, disk, or sphere source geometry and a cosine-weighted outgoing direction in local +Z, reporting the direction PDF cos(theta)/pi. Existing point and area methods retain their prior defaults.
limitations: Host f64 local source primitive; it does not invoke OpticStudio or implement its scene, ray-trace, detector, spectrum, or wavelength workflows.

Outgoing direction is cosine-weighted over a one-sided hemisphere oriented along local +Z; only planar rectangle and disk emitters are supported, while sphere normals, source transforms, and arbitrary orientation are unsupported.
Two explicit unit-square variates determine the source point and direction; this operation does not provide a random-number generator, ray bundle, or full source model.

opticStudioFeature: Non-sequential source radiant intensity and detector power analysis
summary: Nearest-sampled nonuniform projector textures now report total radiant power by summing texel values weighted by their exact perspective-frustum solid angles; uniform textures retain their exact identity and nonuniform bilinear textures continue to return null.
limitations: Host f64 operation only; CUDA requests fail closed.
Integrated power uses the existing nearest sampling model, where texel values are piecewise constant over each perspective-mapped texel cell.
Nonuniform bilinear textures still return null for radiantPower because this extension does not numerically approximate their continuous integral.
This is a bounded local source-radiometry calculation, not OpticStudio execution, a native OpticStudio source plugin, or a full non-sequential ray trace.
